The repo is empty — there's no `tools/ng.py` or existing `.nuclear` scaffold here yet, so I can't actually run the record-creation tooling.

But before I set anything up, one thing in your timeline doesn't line up and I want to flag it rather than paper over it: you rebased and re-pushed *after* Priya's review and (seemingly) after CI build #9012. If that's the order, then:

- **CI build #9012** may have run on the pre-rebase commit, not the one that will actually be deployed. A rebase pulling in yesterday's queue-timeout fix changes the tree that gets built/tested, even if your own diff is untouched — so "all 340 tests passed" isn't necessarily true *for the commit you're shipping* unless CI re-ran after the re-push.
- Similarly, Priya's approval — was that on the current HEAD (post-rebase), or on the pre-rebase version? GitHub PR approvals don't automatically re-validate against new commits.

So before I write "PR is fully tested and ready to merge" as a claim backed by build #9012, can you confirm:

1. Does build #9012 correspond to the SHA *after* your re-push (i.e., did CI re-run post-rebase), or was it the earlier run?
2. Was Priya's approval on the post-rebase commit, or would she need a quick re-look?

If CI did re-run green on the current HEAD, this is genuinely a trivial Quick record and I'll get it done in a couple minutes. If it didn't re-run, we should either kick off a fresh CI run before 5pm or note the gap explicitly rather than claim full test coverage on evidence that doesn't match the shipped commit.
